name: PhoenixSEO Page Builder
author: phoenixseoluebeck

sections.description:
PhoenixSEO Page Builder turns a page into a list of components. A component is a field group — heading, rich text, repeater, link, image — and every component type is its own block in the block inserter, collected under PhoenixSEO components.

The page stores which components it uses and what values they hold, never how they look. Change a component’s markup and every instance on every page changes with it — no per-page migration, and no page carrying a stale copy of the design.

A new component type is a directory, not a new PHP class. Drop sdc-components/card/ with a definition.json in it and the editor, the inserter and the frontend output all handle it, because none of them know about specific types. The file name says nothing about the type — the group key inside it does.

Who this is for

Agencies and developers who build the same page patterns repeatedly (hero, FAQ, feature grid, CTA band) and want them as structured, typed content rather than free-form blocks — with one place that decides what a component looks like.

How it works

  • Every component type is a field group with the key prefix group_sdcpb_component_. The plugin reads those groups from Advanced Custom Fields or Secure Custom Fields.
  • Each type becomes a block (sdcpb/<type>) whose attributes are the field values. Because the block renders on the server, the editor canvas shows the same markup a visitor gets — not a placeholder.
  • The fields are edited in the block sidebar, one form per selected component. Clicking a component in the canvas selects it; the sidebar shows its fields.
  • Content lives in post_content as ordinary block markup, so revisions, autosaves, trash and the REST content API all work the way they do for any block.
  • Component styles are collected into one inline stylesheet in the head, versioned by content hash, so a page load costs one request fewer and aggressive HTML caching stays correct.

Features

  • A block per component type — each component is separately insertable, searchable by its own name, and distinguishable in the list view.
  • The category comes first — PhoenixSEO components sits at the top of the inserter, not somewhere below the core blocks.
  • Server-rendered — the canvas shows the real frontend markup, so a layout bug is visible before the page is published.
  • Component types as JSON schemas — no PHP class per type. Editor, REST layer and frontend are type-agnostic.
  • Only the fields its schema defines — a component accepts exactly its own fields; nothing can be smuggled in as raw HTML by accident.
  • Escaped output — stored values are escaped per field type (esc_html, wp_kses_post, esc_attr); the editor’s data attributes never reach the frontend.
  • Permission-aware — the REST routes check the capability to edit that specific page.
  • Backend overview — a catalogue screen lists every component type with its fields and how many pages use it, and refuses to delete a type that is still placed.
  • i18n-ready — all strings use the text domain phoenixseo-page-builder; a POT file ships in languages/.
  • Your components live in your theme — drop a folder with a JSON field group (and optionally a render.php) into your theme; plugin updates never touch them.

Where do I put my own components?

In your theme, one directory per component:

`

wp-content/themes/your-theme/sdc-components/hero/
definition.json field group (required)
render.php markup (optional)
component.css styles (optional)
`

The plugin also reads the parent theme and wp-content/sdc-components/, so components survive a theme switch when they live in wp-content. The sdcpb_component_dirs filter adds other locations.

Do not add components to the plugin’s own schemas/ directory: it ships the hero and faq examples and is replaced on every update. It follows the same layout — schemas/hero/definition.json.

What are single directory components?

A component whose definition, markup, styles and documentation live in one directory instead of being spread across templates/, css/ and js/. The term comes from Drupal, where it has been part of core since 10.3; the idea behind it is Brad Frost’s Atomic Design (2016, free at atomicdesign.bradfrost.com) and Pattern Lab. One folder per component means one obvious place to look, one thing to copy, and rm -r to remove it.

This plugin borrows the folder discipline, not the whole system. One difference matters: components are siblings in a page’s list, so there are no slots for nesting one component inside another — use the core group block for layout around them.

Can I control the HTML of a component?

Yes, two ways. A render.php next to the component’s JSON renders that component; it receives $type, $data (raw stored values) and $component (the document entry), and can call Sdcpb_Frontend::component_fields_html( $type, $data ) to reuse the default field markup. The sdcpb_component_html filter then has the last word over the finished HTML and can also drop a component by returning an empty string.

Without either, the plugin renders generic markup (div.sdc-component--<type>, one span per field) that a theme styles with CSS.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate either Advanced Custom Fields or Secure Custom Fields. The plugin does nothing without one of them and says so in the admin.
  2. Upload the phoenixseo-page-builder folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  3. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  4. Edit a page, open the inserter and pick a component under PhoenixSEO components.

Pages written by a pre-release version of this plugin, which kept components in a meta row instead of in the content, are converted to blocks the first time they are opened in the editor. The meta row stays as a backup; from then on the editor writes blocks.
sections.faq:
Does it work without Advanced Custom Fields?

No. The plugin uses ACF’s field API for the field definitions. Secure Custom Fields is a drop-in for that API and works the same way. Without either one, the plugin shows an admin notice and stays inert — it does not fatal.

Where is the content stored?

In the post content, as blocks: one <!-- wp:sdcpb/<type> --> comment per component with its field values as attributes. Nothing is kept in a separate table, which is why native revisions, autosaves and the content API include it.

Can two components of the same type be on one page?

Yes, as many as you like. Each block is its own instance with its own attributes.

What about pages from the earlier builder version?

They are converted to blocks the first time they are opened in the editor. Until then they keep rendering from their stored document, so an update in a quiet moment does not lose a page’s content. The conversion is one-way by design: two stores would mean deciding which one wins.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. Component styles are inlined once into the head with a hash-based version, so there is no separate stylesheet URL to go stale after an update, and no extra request per page. By the time a page cache sees the markup it is plain HTML.

What happens if a component type is removed later?

A block can outlive the plugin version that registered it. The editor marks it as unsupported and leaves its saved content alone; the rest of the page still renders. The catalogue screen refuses to delete a type while pages still use it.
sections.changelog:
0.3.3

  • Changed: the component list says which parts of a component exist. The single View file column
    showed only the render template, so a component with styles was indistinguishable from one without,
    and the definition — the file that makes a row exist — had no column at all. Definition, PHP and
    CSS are three columns now, each with a green check or a grey dash and the state in words for a
    screen reader. No extra file reads: the three values are already in the row.
  • Fixed: long file paths break between directories instead of inside definition.json. The browser
    will not break at a slash on its own, so a narrow window cut the filename in half.
  • Fixed: column heads no longer break mid-word on a laptop window. The header cells carry percentage
    widths; a cell’s side padding comes off that percentage, which made Fields wrap as Fiel|ds.

0.3.2

  • Added: the component list can be filtered. All, Templates and Own sit above the table, each
    with a count; one group is hidden when nothing in the site belongs to it. Components that ship with
    the plugin or a theme and components you duplicated sit in one long list otherwise.
  • Added: the code of a shipped component is readable. View Code opens the same three tabs the
    editor has — Definition (JSON), View (PHP), Styles (CSS) — as read-only fields, with the file
    path and a note why nothing can be saved there. The files stay protected: an update would overwrite
    a change. What changed is that reading the PHP and CSS no longer needs FTP, which matters because
    that markup is exactly what you paste into your own copy.
  • Fixed: the row action for a shipped component said Edit and then refused. It now says
    View Code, and the refusal notice is gone.

0.3.1

  • Changed: the plugin is called PhoenixSEO Page Builder. The directory review
    could not accept “SDC Page Builder”: “Page Builder” on its own is generic, and
    “SDC” named neither the plugin nor its author. The text domain follows the name
    and is now phoenixseo-page-builder, the main file is
    phoenixseo-page-builder.php, and the shipped catalogue is
    languages/phoenixseo-page-builder-de_DE.po/.mo. Block names, post meta and
    component folders are unchanged, so an existing site keeps working as it was.

0.3.0

  • Changed: the source strings are English. Before, a plugin installed on an
    English site rendered German — the source language is the fallback, so no
    translation could fix it. Every __() call, the admin screens, the field
    type labels and the example components now speak English, and the catalogue
    ships a German translation in languages/phoenixseo-page-builder-de_DE.po/.mo.
    German sites read exactly as before.
  • Changed: Sdcpb_Field_Editor::TYPES is now definitions(). A constant
    initialiser cannot call __(), so the 54 field type labels, groups and
    choice texts were never translatable — they sat in a const and reached
    the screen as literals.
  • Changed: the example components’ definition.json files are English. Their
    labels live in JSON, which gettext does not reach; a German editor shows
    these demo components in English, and its own components in whatever it
    typed.
  • Fixed: the testimonial quote marks use open-quote/close-quote instead of
    typed German quotation marks, so the browser picks the pair for the
    document’s language.

0.2.2

  • Fixed: a component view that throws no longer takes the page down. Before,
    an exception inside a render.php (a helper that no longer exists, a class
    renamed by an update) surfaced as WordPress’s critical-error page, and the
    cause sat in a log nobody had open. The exception is now caught, the partial
    output is discarded so unbalanced markup cannot break the page’s layout, and
    the failure is logged with its file and line. Visitors get a gap; editors see
    an HTML comment naming the file.
  • Fixed: the migration no longer writes before the permission check. Both
    entry points — the admin edit link and the REST pre-dispatch filter — now
    require edit_post for the post they would touch, instead of relying on a
    check that Core only runs afterwards.
  • Fixed: the source contains no stylesheet or script tag literal any more. The
    guard that rejects the sequence closing an inline stylesheet in a
    component’s CSS builds it from two halves, so a code scanner no longer reads
    the guard as raw output. The plugin delivers its CSS through
    wp_add_inline_style(); it never printed a tag.

0.2.1

  • Fixed: every declaration, option, transient, meta key, hook, block name and
    component group key now carries the sdcpb prefix. Stored data from 0.2.0 is
    moved to the new names automatically on the first request after updating —
    documents, block delimiters and component JSON definitions — so existing pages
    keep rendering. wp sdc-pb rename --dry-run shows what the move would touch.
  • Fixed: upload metadata is validated as scalar values and checked against
    UPLOAD_ERR_OK before it is used, which removes a PHP 8 TypeError on a
    malformed upload.
  • Fixed: file operations go through wp_delete_file() and wp_is_writable()
    instead of unlink() and is_writable().
  • Fixed: a forced component import reads its flag through sanitize_key().
  • Removed: load_plugin_textdomain(). wordpress.org loads the text domain
    itself, so the call only loaded the same catalogue a second time.
  • New: ten example components ship with the plugin — a record, a film and a
    series that show what a component can do, plus seven general-purpose ones
    (hero, feature grid, statistics, pricing table, testimonials, CTA band, FAQ).
    They are examples, referred to by the same directory mechanism any own
    component uses.
  • New: three screenshots of the rendered examples.

0.2.0

  • New: the component screen carries a credit line with the author’s site and a
    donation link. Sites that resell the plugin can remove it with the
    sdcpb_credit filter; it appears only on this plugin’s own screen.
  • Fixed: converting a pre-block page to blocks could drop components. The
    conversion now adds each missing component instance instead of only flagging
    the page as converted, so a page never loses a component on its way from the
    old store to block markup.
  • New: wp sdc-pb repair [--post=<id>] [--apply] finds pages whose stored
    document and block content disagree. It is a dry run by default; --apply
    writes the missing blocks. Idempotent — a second run reports nothing to do.
  • New: a component whose view file is missing or no longer renders now says so.
    The failure is logged once per request and type instead of disappearing, and
    editors — never visitors — see a marker in the rendered page and a notice on
    the pages list.

0.1.0

  • Initial release.
  • One block per component type, registered from the component’s JSON definition.
  • A dedicated PhoenixSEO components block category, first in the inserter.
  • Server-side rendering, so the editor canvas shows the frontend markup.
  • Component types defined as JSON schemas; editor, REST and frontend are type-agnostic.
  • Field editing in the block sidebar; click a component to select it.
  • One-way conversion of documents from the pre-block version into blocks, with the meta row kept as a backup.
  • Host parity between Advanced Custom Fields (free) and Secure Custom Fields.
  • Catalogue screen with per-type usage counts and a delete guard.
  • Inline, hash-versioned component styles for cache-safe delivery.
  • German source strings, POT file, and translation loading on init.

short_description: Reusable page components as native blocks: pick one from the inserter, edit its fields in the sidebar, see the real markup in the canvas.

screenshots.caption: A record component: the track number comes from the row order and the total running time is added up from the durations — neither is a field.
A film component: facts as a definition list, the rating as a <meter>, the running time written from a number of minutes.
A series component: every season is a <details> element, folded away by default and usable from the keyboard without JavaScript.
